literature.summary: The Pan European Games Information (PEGI) system is an age-based rating system for interactive games in Europe, developed by the industry and administered by a non-governmental organization. Although voluntary, console manufacturers and most UK retailers require games to be rated by PEGI or the BBFC (for 18-rated games). There is a recommendation for future reforms to extend the statutory basis to include video games that would typically receive a 12+ PEGI rating and to establish a single classification system, as consumers, particularly parents, sometimes misunderstand the PEGI ratings.

literature.summary: Computer games classification is largely self-regulated by industry bodies like the Electronic Software Ratings Board (ESRB) in the US and PEGI in Europe. While participation is voluntary, major retailers often only carry rated copies of games. An attempt in California to make ESRB prohibitions on the sale of M or AO-rated games to children legally enforceable was deemed unconstitutional.
